title: 4-round AES-128: two-set square, complete-key claim

target.description: AES-128 on 128-bit blocks, reduced to 4 rounds. Lucks includes MixColumns in the final round (Section 2.2 footnote). Equivalent subkey L^r=ShiftRows^-1(MixColumns^-1(K^r)); this is not the final-no-MixColumns convention used by FKLSSWW. A second Lambda1 set filters the fourth-round subkey candidates and thereby determines the AES-128 master key.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key; no related-key or known-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no restriction to a weak-key family
setting.plaintext_model: Two independently chosen Lambda1 structures of 256 plaintexts each.
assumptions: A wrong integral subkey guess is modeled as passing an eight-bit balance check with probability about 2^-8; repeated checks use the source's heuristic filtering assumptions.

time.note: The paragraph gives about 2^20 dominant byte XORs for either candidate-completion alternative; the rough estimate does not itemize a factor for the extra structure.

data.note: The source explicitly doubles the one-set data for the second-structure alternative.

memory.note: The source describes small storage for the four/five-round algorithms but supplies no numeric whole-procedure peak.

preprocessing.note: The paper does not separately price setup for this endpoint.

success.description: Section3.1 states that the full key is uniquely determined with overwhelming probability, either by exhaustive testing on the first256 known pairs or by a second256-text Lambda set. This is a qualitative author statement, not a numerical rate. The expected fewer than2^16 surviving keys and per-wrong-byte2^-8 filter do not specify complete-key success at either recorded data budget.

review.scope: Both four-round completion routes checked in the exact AES3 chapter. The source's qualitative overwhelming-probability statement is positively retained; no exact100%, independent-set product or finite-transcript uniqueness bound is inferred. Existing native byte-XOR cost, Lambda filters, coordinate conflicts and full-audit gates unchanged.

components.description: Chapter7–13 Eq.(3)/Sections3–6: the necessary balance relation holds under the correct hypothesis in the intended Square construction. Existing ShiftRows/printed-coordinate conflicts mean this is not a certification of the literal implementation.
Chapter7 Section3.1: an incorrect L4 byte passes one balance test with source probability2^-8. Less than2^16 candidate keys is an expectation, not a deterministic list bound.

The general BO definition on chapter p8 omits the previous inverse ShiftRows column adjustment for a nonzero target row. For SR(A)(i,j)=A(i,j+s*i), BO input column j and row k require the previous L byte at (k,j+s*k). The surrounding row-0 constructions avoid this adjustment. Independent finite controls check local algebra, not a complete attack repair.

field_conflicts.label: ShiftRows formula and diagram coordinates
field_conflicts.description: Chapterp3 defines left-going SR, B(i,j)=A(i,j+i), but Fig2 and Table1 use right-going coordinates. The later anti-diagonal reaches columns0/2 under the literal left formula and one column under the right diagram. A coherent coordinate convention must be selected before reproducing the printed algorithm. This does not refute the direction-independent integral or establish a standard-key-schedule reflection equivalence.
